items.title: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack") Interview, 1959-07-01
items.q: Did you play or sing with Robichaux out there? Yes. I know he played there for many years.

ctx.x: And Robichaux's music was kind of a classic kind, you know. Mm-hmm. He didn't, uh, like jazz. Yes, that's right. He didn't jazz much, you know. And any theatre that we went to that had an orchestra, when, uh, they played their overture. They threw in their wheelchairs. Mm-hmm. That's right. Uh-huh.
And Robichaux was crazy about our style, though, and our music. Yeah. He didn't sit back and pull it wrong. Yeah. That was a, you could see him shaking and laughing off. Oh, for sure.

I might ask you just a minute or two, Mr. Mack, about, uh, the music in Mobile. I've heard of the old Excelsior Brass Band, and, uh, we talked to Mr. Pope, not the, I can't think of his first name. Alexander Pope was the leader of the original band. Yeah. And I talked to his son, who's still living. He's about 80 years old now.
